Do supersonic winds on planets cause long-lasting sonic booms?
My scientific contribution to the conversation is that THAT WOULD BE BADASS.

You can't have supersonic wind. It defies the very definition of itself.

Supersonic refers to speeds greater than the speed of sound (pressure waves) in a medium. A medium can't travel faster than it's maximum propagation speed; it's a completely contradictory and nonsensical statement/question.

Sonic booms are created by objects traveling through a medium faster than the speed of sound in that medium. Not the medium itself (which also can't flow faster than it's maximum speed...)
So winds in gas giants' atmospheres can't go faster than sound?

When you say something is going faster than the speed of sound, that speed is being measured relative to the atmosphere. Wind is movement of the atmosphere itself, so super-sonic wind doesn't make sense. The wind's speed relative to itself is always 0.

The closest thing you could have is extremely turbulent wind where there is a steep gradient of velocities, where some part of the atmosphere is moving supersonically through some other part close by.
correct. however, the speed of sound is different on different planets (and in different regions of space), as the sound speed depends upon: temperature, pressure, density.

Search Risk: How Google Almost Killed ProtonMail | ProtonMail

The short summary is that for nearly a year, Google was hiding ProtonMail from search results for queries such as ‘secure email’ and ‘encrypted email’. This was highly suspicious because ProtonMail has long been the world’s largest encrypted email provider.

[...]

In November 2015, we became aware of the problem and consulted a number of well known SEO experts. None of them could explain the issue, especially since ProtonMail has never used any blackhat SEO tactics, nor did we observe any used against us. Mysteriously, the issue was entirely limited to Google, as this anomaly was not seen on any other search engine.

[...]

This incident however highlights a previously unrecognized danger that we are now calling Search Risk. The danger is that any service such as ProtonMail can easily be suppressed by either search companies, or the governments that control those search companies. This can happen even across national borders. For example, even though Google is an American company, it controls over 90% of European search traffic. In this case, Google directly caused ProtonMail’s growth rate worldwide to be reduced by over 25% for over 10 months.
